title: Trust your experience.
subtitle: Feelings are data.
criticalLine: Challenge models that exclude you or ask you to be someone else.

critiques.text: Mainstream science should examine subjective experience, not dismiss it in advance. Explaining what the brain does does not, by itself, explain why there is something it feels like to be you.
Physicalism proposes that everything, including mind, is physical. Does the evidence establish that worldview, or is the worldview deciding which evidence counts? Keep the question open.

Secular humanism values reason, experience, and human flourishing. Hold it to those commitments: when experience challenges its assumptions, is it investigated or explained away? A worldview must answer to inquiry, too.

loveDefinition: Love is the condition in which Fear no longer governs you.
invitation: Read the book. Examine your experience. Ask questions, and be willing to change what you hold to be true. This work can be long and difficult. Take your time; there is no timetable for it.
boundary: Henok’s account begins with lived experience. His explanations of a larger consciousness and a nonphysical substrate remain hypotheses, open to challenge and revision.
edition: Book One is a fixed edition. The Academy holds definitions and open questions as the inquiry develops.
